contributions: Open access textbook on game theory with no cost barrier
165 exercises with complete and detailed solutions across all chapters
An alternative state-space approach to incomplete information that avoids the conventional type-space formalism
A conceptual framework for perfect Bayesian equilibrium anchored in AGM belief revision theory
limitations: The author acknowledges that there will likely be typos and possibly minor mistakes in the text. The book is self-described as not filling a strict need since many excellent game theory textbooks already exist. The rigorous treatment with proofs, while intentional, may present challenges despite claiming accessibility with only high-school-level mathematics.
methods: The book is structured as a textbook covering game theory from foundational to advanced levels. Part I covers ordinal-payoff games in strategic, perfect-information dynamic, and imperfect-information dynamic forms. Part II addresses cardinal payoffs, expected utility, and mixed-strategy equilibria. Parts III-V cover knowledge and belief, equilibrium refinements in dynamic games (weak sequential, sequential, and perfect Bayesian equilibrium), and incomplete information using a state-space approach rather than the conventional Harsanyi type-space framework.
results: The textbook contains 165 exercises with full solutions distributed across all chapters, each section includes exercises and each chapter concludes with a challenging question. The book covers 15 chapters plus appendices. It emphasizes that rational choice depends on player preferences rather than assuming selfishness, demonstrating this through the Split or Steal example where a fair-minded player would choose differently than a selfish one. The state-space approach to incomplete information is presented as simpler and more elegant than the type-space approach, with equivalence shown between the two.
tldr: An open access game theory textbook containing 165 solved exercises, designed to be accessible with only high-school-level mathematics and covering both ordinal and cardinal games across five parts.
